plan.title: Publish VSCode Extension to GitHub Packages
plan.overview: Create an installer script for the VSCode extension that can be invoked via npx @mattfletcher94/claudeban-vscode. The installer locates the bundled .vsix file and runs code --install-extension, following the exact pattern established in apps/kanban/bin/install.cjs with ANSI-colored CLI output.

approach.rationale:
Following two established patterns: - CLI installer structure: apps/kanban/bin/install.cjs:1-132 provides the exact template for ANSI colors, parseArgs, showHelp, showVersion, and main() structure - Package publishConfig: apps/kanban/package.json:35-38 shows the GitHub Packages registry configuration
The installer is simpler than the kanban installer because it only needs to: 1. Find the .vsix file (embedded in the package) 2. Run code --install-extension to install it 3. Show success message with next steps
No file copying or directory creation needed unlike the kanban installer.

task.name: Create installer script
task.requirements: FR1, FR2, FR3, FR4, FR5, FR6, FR7, FR8
task.done: Script runs, shows help text with correct package name and usage

task.name: Configure package.json for publishing
task.action:
Add to apps/vscode/package.json: - Change "name" from "claude-kanban-vscode" to "@mattfletcher94/claudeban-vscode" - Add "bin" field pointing to bin/install.cjs - Add "files" array including bin/ and the .vsix file - Add "repository" field - Add "publishConfig" with GitHub Packages registry
Current package.json name: ```json "name": "claude-kanban-vscode", ```
Change to: ```json "name": "@mattfletcher94/claudeban-vscode", "bin": { "claudeban-vscode": "bin/install.cjs" }, "files": [ "bin", "claude-kanban-vscode-*.vsix" ], "repository": { "type": "git", "url": "https://github.com/mattfletcher94/claudeban" }, "publishConfig": { "registry": "https://npm.pkg.github.com", "access": "restricted" }, ```
Note: prepublishOnly hook not needed - .vsix is already built by vscode:package
task.done: package.json has scoped name, bin, files, repository, and publishConfig

task.name: Add vscode:publish script to root
task.action:
Add vscode:publish script to root package.json scripts:
Current: ```json "vscode:install": "pnpm vscode:package && code --install-extension apps/vscode/claude-kanban-vscode-0.1.0.vsix" ```
Add after vscode:install: ```json "vscode:publish": "pnpm --filter @mattfletcher94/claudeban-vscode publish --no-git-checks" ```

task.name: Test installer locally
task.requirements: FR2, FR3, FR4, FR5, FR6, FR7, FR8
task.action: Manual verification: 1. Run: node apps/vscode/bin/install.cjs --help - Verify usage shows npx @mattfletcher94/claudeban-vscode - Verify options show -h/--help and -v/--version 2. Run: node apps/vscode/bin/install.cjs --version - Verify version number is shown 3. Run: node apps/vscode/bin/install.cjs - Verify it finds the .vsix file - Verify it runs code --install-extension - Verify ANSI colors are displayed (cyan header, green success) - Verify next steps are shown after success 4. Test error handling: - Temporarily rename the .vsix file - Run installer, verify error is shown - Restore the .vsix file
task.done: Installer works locally with all flags and handles errors

testing.automated: None - simple CLI script, manual verification sufficient
testing.manual: - Run installer with --help flag, verify usage is correct - Run installer with --version flag, verify version is shown - Run installer without flags, verify extension installs - Verify ANSI colors are displayed correctly in terminal - Verify next steps message is shown after success
testing.regression: Verify existing vscode:package script still works

edge-cases.case: Let error propagate naturally - user sees clear error message from the system
Show error with path where file was expected
code --install-extension handles this gracefully, shows "already installed" message

pitfalls.pitfall: Use glob pattern claude-kanban-vscode-*.vsix relative to package directory, not hardcoded version
Read from package.json version field, not hardcode it
